parts: Lesson 28: Differentiation of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions — Summary
d/dx eˣ = eˣ; d/dx aˣ = aˣ log a; d/dx log x = 1/x (x > 0). With the chain rule: d/dx e^(f(x)) = e^(f(x)) f'(x) and d/dx log f(x) = f'(x)/f(x). For example d/dx log(2x + 3) = 2/(2x + 3).
Simplify first: e^(−3 log x) = x⁻³, so its derivative is −3x⁻⁴.
For y = u^v (variable base and power), take logs: log y = v log u, then differentiate: (1/y) dy/dx = v' log u + v u'/u. Example: d/dx(xˣ) = xˣ(1 + log x).
For y = Ae^(kx) + Be^(−kx), y'' = k²y. Example: y = 500e^(7x) + 600e^(−7x) gives y'' = 49y.
Derivative of sin x with respect to log x = (cos x)/(1/x) = x cos x.
